question: A sound wave with a period of 0.01 seconds has a frequency of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**100 Hz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The relationship between frequency and period is defined as **Frequency = 1 / Period**.
 
• A sound wave with a period of 0.01 seconds has a frequency calculated as **1 / 0.01 = 100 Hz**.
 
• Frequency is measured in **Hertz (Hz)**, which represents the number of cycles per second.
 
• Sound waves with a frequency of 100 Hz fall within the range of **human hearing, typically between 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.**
 
• The period and frequency are inversely related—if the period is short, the frequency is high, and vice versa.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frequency:**

 
 
• Frequency refers to the number of oscillations or cycles a wave completes in one second.
 
• It is measured in Hertz (Hz), where 1 Hz equals one cycle per second.
 
 
 
• **Period:**
 
 
• The period is the time taken for one complete cycle of a wave.
 
• It is expressed in seconds and is the reciprocal of frequency.
 
 
 
• **Sound Waves:**
 
 
• Sound waves are longitudinal waves that travel through a medium (air, water, solids).
 
• They consist of compressions and rarefactions caused by vibrating objects.
 
 
 
• **Human Hearing Range:**
 
 
• Humans can typically hear frequencies ranging from 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz.
 
• Frequencies below 20 Hz are called infrasonic, and frequencies above 20,000 Hz are ultrasonic.
